newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen flat as foreigners sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen flat as foreigners sidelined.

text.p: Thai stocks were seen softer on Friday as some foreigners were expected to remain sidelined after latest central bank's measures to cut off foreign baht repatriation from deals through the bourse, brokers said.
"I don't think foreign investors will come back to the market today. The measures have significantly reduced their interest to trade in shares," said one broker at Thaimex Finance and Securities.

New measures announced by the Bank of Thailand on Tuesday required bank custodians not to accept transfers of borrowed and unpaid stocks from foreigners and non-resident investors selling Thai stocks must remit funds in foreign currencies only.
The measures were imposed to cut off supply sources for baht speculators following the last attack on the baht in mid-May.
The composite SET index on Thursday ended 1.64 points lower at 519.76 on 3.2 billion baht turnover.
